challenge.title: Can your design survive IND vs PAK?
challenge.desc: On 14 October 2023, 3.5 crore people watched India play Pakistan live on one streaming app, all at the same time. You run the video servers tonight. Set them up and play the match.

options.label: No CDN
options.desc: Every viewer streams from your servers.

options.label: CDN, 90% from the edge
options.desc: Servers near the viewers keep the video; 1 request in 10 reaches yours.

options.label: CDN, 98% from the edge
options.desc: A well-tuned CDN: 1 request in 50 reaches your servers.

options.label: Autoscale
options.desc: Start small and add servers as viewers arrive. New ones take 5 minutes to boot.

options.label: Start them all before the toss
options.desc: Pay for every server from the start, so nothing has to boot mid-match.

challenge.survived: You survived. Every viewer got the last over.
challenge.failed: Buffering for {crore} crore viewers around the {moment}. {minutes} minutes with buffering in all.
challenge.noCdn: Without a CDN the last over needs {servers} servers sending {tbps} Tbps from one origin. Nobody does that: add a CDN.
challenge.cta: Build it properly in the Lab
challenge.note: Viewer curve: a typical close evening match, peaking at the 3.5 crore record (ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023, India vs Pakistan, as reported by the broadcaster). The app here is made up. 2 Mbps a viewer, 10 Gbps and about $0.50 an hour a server, and CDN shares are rules of thumb, not measurements.

fact.title: One of the busiest websites on Earth is an adult video site.
fact.desc: It reported about 115 million visits a day in 2019, and in 2018 it sent 4,403 petabytes of video: roughly 147 GB every second, busiest late at night. Here is how a site like that stays up.
points: Each video is split into pieces a few seconds long, in several qualities. Any server can send any piece, and a player can switch quality between pieces when the network slows.
The CDN does the heavy lifting
Servers in hundreds of cities keep the popular pieces close to viewers. Almost every request ends there; the company's own servers see a small share.
Plan for the peak, not the average
Traffic is far higher at night than in the afternoon. Capacity is sized for the busiest hour, and the CDN absorbs the surges.
fact.source: Figures from the site's own published yearly reports for 2018 and 2019.
